alert_details.headline: Small Craft Advisory issued November 19 at 2:37AM PST until November 19 at 3:00PM PST
alert_details.description:
* WHAT...West winds 15 to 25 kt with gusts up to 30 kt and seas
8 to 13 ft.

* WHERE...Coastal Waters from Point Reyes to Pigeon Point
California out to 10 NM.

* WHEN...Until 3 PM PST this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Conditions will be hazardous to small craft.

alert_details.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 19 at 5:55AM PST until November 20 at 1:00AM PST
alert_details.description:
* WHAT...Large breaking waves of 15 to 18 ft.

* WHERE...All Pacific Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...Until 1 AM PST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Large breaking waves can overpower swimmers, pulling
people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks resulting
in significant physical injury and increasing the risk of
drowning. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without
warning, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties,
and rocks.

alert_details.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 19 at 5:55AM PST until November 20 at 1:00AM PST
alert_details.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to 1.2 ft of
inundation above ground level is likely in low-lying areas near
shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...North Bay Interior Valleys and San Francisco Bay
Shoreline Counties.

* WHEN...For the first Coastal Flood Advisory, until 10 AM PST
Friday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high
tide is expected to be 1.2 ft above normal (7.0 ft MLLW) at
7:15 AM Thursday and 1.1 ft above normal (6.9 ft MLLW) at 7:45
AM Friday. These predictions include up to 1.8 ft of surge
that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the
Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.

sources: Open-Meteo forecast + marine, NOAA CO-OPS tides and water temperature, NWS alerts
